steps.name: LRT for condition-by-time interaction (treatment-specific temporal change)
steps.question: Which of the 12000 genes show a statistically significant condition:time interaction — i.e. a temporal trajectory across t0..t3 that differs between the two treatment conditions, beyond whatever time trend is shared by both conditions?

grounding.reason: DESeq2 full-vs-reduced-model LRT for time-course interaction terms is the package's documented method for this exact question (DESeq2 vignette, time-series section); no knowledge_recommend tool was attached this run to produce citable claim IDs.

acceptance_criteria: DESeq2 is run with full design ~condition + time + condition:time and reduced design ~condition + time, using test='LRT' so the interaction term alone is tested
time is treated as a categorical factor with 4 levels (t0,t1,t2,t3) matching the metadata, not as a continuous covariate, since the design has exactly 4 sampled time points per condition
Independent filtering and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction are applied via DESeq2's results() with padj reported for every gene

Output table includes gene symbol, LRT statistic, raw p-value, padj, and the per-timepoint interaction coefficients (or equivalent contrast estimates) so direction and magnitude of condition-specific change are recoverable

The number of genes significant at padj < 0.05 is reported, and the result is distinguished from genes significant for the condition main effect or time main effect alone (those are not the same test and must not be conflated in the writeup)

grounding.reason: Model-based clustering (mclust) applied to condition-difference trajectories as a descriptive step; no specific method paper searched matched this exact use, treated as standard exploratory clustering.

acceptance_criteria: Uses only genes passing the LRT interaction FDR threshold from T1S2 (analysis is not repeated on the full 12000-gene set)

plan.title: DESeq2 LRT for condition-by-time interaction effects
plan.analytical_narrative: The design is 2 conditions x 4 time points (t0-t3) x 3 replicates (24 samples, 12000 genes, raw salmon counts). The research question — which genes change over time in a condition-specific way, beyond the trend shared by both conditions — is precisely the condition:time interaction term in a factorial time-course model. The standard, well-established approach (documented in the DESeq2 vignette's time-course section, Love/Huber/Anders 2014, Genome Biology) is a likelihood-ratio test comparing a full model (~condition + time + condition:time) against a reduced model that drops only the interaction (~condition + time): genes with significant LRT p-values are those whose temporal trajectory differs by condition, independent of any main effect of condition or of the shared time trend. After identifying this gene set, its members are characterized by extracting per-condition fitted/normalized trajectories and grouping them into pattern classes (e.g. divergence starting early vs late, transient vs sustained, crossover vs parallel-shift) using variance-stabilized expression, and interpreted via pathway enrichment against WikiPathways human and MSigDB Hallmark gene sets, both available for Homo sapiens in the reference store. Steps are ordered so QC/normalization precedes the interaction test, which precedes both pattern characterization and enrichment (the latter two can run in parallel off the same gene list).
